newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * The government holds talks with International Monetary Fund experts aimed at reaching new loan accord. IMF chief negotiator for Romania, Poul Thomsen, is attending.
* Bucharest will host Romanian-Hungarian consultations on implementation of the treaty signed last year, foreign ministry spokesman Sorin Ducaru told a news conference.
Talks are expected to focus on setting up a bilateral commission for the treaty's implementation and on opening consular offices in the neighbouring countries, he said.

* Ducaru said British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind is expected for a two-day visit to Romania starting January 27, to discuss bilateral ties and Romania's efforts to gain early NATO admission. Rifkind and his Romanian counterpart, Adrian Severin, will hold a joint news conference on January 28.

* Foreign ministry secretaries of state Dumitru Ciausu and Lazar Comanescu will leave on diplomatic missions to Bonn and, respectively, Ottawa, as part of Bucharest's lobby to be included among the first countries invited to join NATO.
* European Integration Minister Alexandru Herlea will visit France ahead of President Jacques Chirac's visit to Romania scheduled for end-February, a ministry statement said.
It said Herlea will advocate Romania's market reforms and its efforts to prepare for integration into the European Union.
* Lower Chamber of Deputies holds debates on the teaching staff draft law. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
